knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The lesson says the rate is built by dividing running costs and income by billable hours, so the work that can be billed covers them. Using all paid hours, a competitor's rate or a wished-for rate does not do this.
The lesson says travel, set-up and admin time do not shrink with the size of the job, so a minimum charge covers the visit. It does not replace a written quote.
The lesson says to use local evidence and the owner's own costs and billable hours. A single national average, a friend's rate or a bidding-site listing is not a sound check on its own.

practicalCriteria: Learner calculates billable hours from a one-month log, showing each non-billable deduction.
Learner builds a base rate from a worksheet of annual costs and an income target, showing the calculation.
Learner sets a minimum charge for a short job and writes the wording the client will see before the visit.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
stopWorkCriteria: Stop work if procedure step 1 is not done: Estimate the paid working hours in a year, then subtract travel, quoting, admin, marketing, training and leave to find the billable hours.
